problem: Loopbreaker's domain rules — behavior children enforced by default, the three-pass cap, freeze on approval, review-completion separate from ship-readiness — live only in code. A held gate can't cite the invariant it enforces and the UI can't show why a gate held, so the reasoning is opaque to both humans and agents.
appetite: One read-only canon slice; enforcement semantics stay in domain.ts.
smallest_slice: Add a canon table of seeded invariant nodes and have each held gate reason reference the canon id it enforces, shown in the visualizer inspector.
non_goals: The claim calculus: computed status from evaluators, justification edges, coherence axes
Editing enforcement semantics from data — the rules remain in domain.ts
Canon domains, tiers, and register axes (stay in Rordi)
success_signal: The core invariants are seeded and listable, and every held gate reason carries a real canon id whose statement the inspector renders.
reversibility: Canon is read-only and additive; removing the citation disables the feature without affecting any gate.

risks.risk: Canon text drifts from the code rules it documents.
risks.mitigation: Seed from a single source and test that each gate cites a real canon id.
